doc.summary: Deletes multiple mail records from the database using a prepared SQL DELETE statement.
doc.overview: This function constructs a dynamic SQL query to remove specified mail entries based on an array of unique identifiers. It iterates through the provided buffer vector, formatting each ID into a comma-separated list for the IN clause before executing the deletion via CharacterDatabase.Execute().

params.name: buffer
params.desc: A vector containing the unique IDs of mail records to be deleted.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure all IDs in buffer are valid and exist in the mail table to avoid unnecessary operations or potential SQL errors if validation is not handled elsewhere.

doc.summary: Validates and executes a guild task transfer by checking if the bot is a random shadow, verifying text matches the new owner's character name, and migrating active tasks to the new owner.
doc.overview: This function first performs strict validation on the bot entity, ensuring it belongs to a valid guild and is registered as a random shadow before proceeding. It then queries the database for all characters associated with the original owner's account to identify potential new owners. If a matching character name is found within the provided text, the function transfers specific task values (active, item, and kill tasks) from the old owner to the new owner while resetting the old owner's task status.

params.name: text
params.desc: The search string used to match the name of the potential new owner character.

params.name: ownerPlayer
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the current owner of the guild task.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot attempting to transfer the task.

doc.side_effects: Database queries, global state updates via SetTaskValue, and network message sending via SendCompletionMessage.
doc.notes: Returns false if the bot is invalid or lacks a guild; returns true only after successfully transferring tasks or completing validation without transfer.

doc.summary: Manages guild-specific tasks such as item collection and creature kills, handling creation, tracking, completion rewards, and advertisement notifications.
doc.overview: The GuildTaskMgr class serves as the central controller for all guild-related task mechanics within the game server. It provides functionality to create, track, and complete various tasks like gathering items or defeating specific creatures, while automatically notifying guild members via advertisements when tasks are fulfilled. The system integrates with the database through transaction objects to persist task data and manage rewards.
doc.side_effects: Database transactions (CharacterDatabaseTransaction), network I/O for advertisements and messages, global state updates via singleton instance
doc.notes: Callers must ensure database transactions are properly managed when invoking methods like SendAdvertisement or Reward. Edge cases include handling duplicate advertisements and managing task expiration logic within GetTaskValues.

doc.summary: Finds the first occurrence of a case-insensitive substring within a string and returns a pointer to it.
doc.overview: This function performs a case-insensitive search for the needle string within the haystack string. It iterates through the haystack, comparing characters using lowercase conversion to match the needle, and returns a pointer to the starting position of the first match if found. If no match is discovered or either input string is null, it returns a null pointer.

params.name: haystack
params.desc: Pointer to the string in which to search.

params.name: needle
params.desc: Pointer to the substring to search for.

doc.notes: Returns a pointer to the start of the match; if no match is found, returns NULL. Caller must ensure null safety when dereferencing the returned pointer.

doc.summary: Removes leading whitespace characters from the beginning of a string in place.
doc.overview: This function modifies the input string by erasing all leading spaces, tabs, and other whitespace characters until it encounters the first non-whitespace character. It returns a reference to the modified string, allowing for immediate use without additional assignment steps. The operation is efficient as it only processes characters from the start of the string.

params.name: s
params.desc: The input string whose leading whitespace will be removed.

doc.side_effects: Modifies the content of the input string in place.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the reference is valid before calling. If the string contains only whitespace, it will be emptied. No global state or I/O operations are performed.

doc.summary: Removes trailing whitespace from the input string in-place and returns a reference to it.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the string from right to left to locate the last non-whitespace character. It then erases all characters following that position, effectively stripping any spaces, tabs, or newlines at the end of the string. The operation modifies the original string directly without creating a copy.

params.name: s
params.desc: The input string by reference to be modified.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure the string is not empty before calling, as `std::find_if` on an empty range returns `s.rend()`, resulting in undefined behavior when erasing from `s.rend()` to `s.end()`.

doc.summary: Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string in-place by delegating to left and right trim operations.
doc.overview: This function takes a reference to a std::string and returns the same object with all leading and trailing whitespace characters removed. It achieves this by first applying right trim to strip trailing spaces, then applying left trim to remove any leading spaces from the result. The operation modifies the original string directly without creating a new copy.

params.name: s
params.desc: A reference to a std::string object whose whitespace will be trimmed in-place.

doc.notes: The function modifies the input string directly. It assumes valid C++ string objects and does not handle null pointers or invalid memory states.

doc.summary: Splits a string into a vector of substrings based on a delimiter character.
doc.overview: This function takes a string and a delimiter character, then separates the string into individual words using that delimiter. It populates the provided destination vector with these substrings in order. The implementation uses strtok to parse the input, which modifies the original string passed by reference.

params.name: dest
params.desc: A reference to a std::vector<std::string> that will be populated with the split substrings.

params.name: str
params.desc: The input string to be split into parts.

params.name: delim
params.desc: A C-style character pointer representing the delimiter character used for splitting.

doc.side_effects: modifies dest, I/O (via strdup and free)
doc.notes: The function modifies the input string 'str' in place by using strtok. It is not thread-safe due to the use of strtok and shared memory modification.

doc.summary: Splits a string into a vector of substrings based on a delimiter character.
doc.overview: This function takes a string and a delimiter character, then uses std::stringstream to parse the input string into individual components. Each component is extracted using getline until no more data remains, with each part being appended to the provided output vector. The function returns a reference to this populated vector, allowing the caller to access the split results directly.

params.name: s
params.desc: The input string to be split.

params.name: delim
params.desc: The character used as a delimiter to separate elements in the string.

params.name: elems
params.desc: A reference to a vector where the split substrings will be stored.

doc.notes: The function modifies the elems vector in place. It relies on std::stringstream, which may have performance implications for very large strings due to temporary allocations.

doc.summary: Splits a string into a vector of substrings based on a delimiter character.
doc.overview: This function takes a string and a delimiter character, then separates the string at every occurrence of that delimiter. It returns a vector containing all the resulting substrings in order. The implementation delegates the actual splitting logic to an overloaded version that accepts a reference to the output container.

params.name: s
params.desc: The input string to be split.

params.name: delim
params.desc: The character used as the delimiter for splitting.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the input string is not empty if they expect non-empty results. The function does not modify the input string.

doc.summary: A template class that defers computation of a value until it is requested, storing the result to avoid redundant calculations.
doc.overview: LazyCalculatedValue encapsulates a callable method on an owner object and delays its execution until GetValue() is invoked. This pattern optimizes performance by preventing unnecessary computations when the value is not immediately needed, while ensuring thread safety through atomic-like state management of the calculated flag. The class manages the lifecycle of the computed result internally, allowing the caller to retrieve a cached value or reset the cache for recalculation.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure TOwner* is valid before construction. Reset() invalidates the cached value, requiring recomputation on next access.

doc.summary: Constructs a new LootTarget object by copying the GUID and timestamp from another LootTarget instance.
doc.overview: This function implements the copy constructor for the LootTarget class, creating a deep or shallow copy depending on implementation details. It initializes the internal state of the new object with the exact values provided by the source argument, ensuring data integrity during object duplication. This is typically invoked implicitly when a LootTarget variable is assigned to another or passed by value.

params.name: other
params.desc: The source LootTarget instance whose GUID and asOfTime will be copied.

doc.notes: Callers should expect the new object to have identical GUID and timestamp values; no external state is modified.

doc.summary: Compares two LootTarget instances by their GUIDs to determine ordering.
doc.overview: This operator implements a strict weak ordering for LootTarget objects based solely on the comparison of their unique identifiers (guid). It returns true if the current object's guid is less than the other object's guid, facilitating sorted containers and binary search operations within the loot system. The implementation assumes that GUIDs are globally unique and sufficient to distinguish between different loot targets.

params.name: other
params.desc: A const reference to another LootTarget instance whose GUID will be compared against this object's GUID.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure they are using this operator when sorting LootTarget vectors or sets. Edge case: if two targets share the same GUID (which violates uniqueness assumptions), the result is undefined behavior.

doc.summary: Removes all LootTarget entries from the stack whose associated time is less than or equal to the specified cutoff.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the LootObjectStack and removes any LootTarget objects that have an 'asOfTime' value less than or equal to the provided fromTime parameter. It uses a single-pass algorithm with direct iterator manipulation to efficiently prune outdated entries without creating temporary containers.

params.name: fromTime
params.desc: The time threshold; any LootTarget with an asOfTime less than or equal to this value will be removed.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure fromTime is a valid time_t value; the function assumes the stack contains only LootTarget objects and does not handle other types.

doc.overview: This constructor initializes a LootObject with a provided player bot and object GUID, setting skill requirements to zero. It immediately triggers a refresh operation to populate the object's attributes from the server database. The resulting object is ready for use in loot management systems without requiring further setup.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player entity that owns or interacts with this loot object.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The unique identifier of the object being created, used to fetch its data from the server.

doc.notes: Calls Refresh() synchronously; may block if the server is unreachable. Ensure bot pointer is valid before construction.

doc.summary: Determines if a player bot can loot a specific creature or game object based on skill requirements, quest item restrictions, and lock mechanisms.
doc.overview: This function evaluates whether a given bot is permitted to collect items from a target entity identified by its GUID. It first checks for corpse creatures, verifying they are lootable and meeting specific skill thresholds derived from the creature's level and template. If the target is a game object, it analyzes quest item composition and loot templates to ensure only valid quest items are available or that the bot possesses necessary keys or skills. Finally, it processes various lock types associated with the game object to grant access if conditions are met.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the player bot instance performing the action.

params.name: lootGUID
params.desc: The unique identifier of the creature or game object intended for looting.

doc.notes: Modifies internal state variables (skillId, reqSkillValue, reqItem) within the calling context; returns early if the bot lacks AI capabilities or if specific lock conditions are not satisfied.

doc.summary: Determines whether a specific item ID is required to complete any incomplete quest currently held by the bot.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all active quests in the bot's log, checking each for incomplete status and verifying if the provided item ID matches an unfulfilled objective. It returns true immediately upon finding a matching requirement within any of the bot's current quests, otherwise it returns false after exhausting all quest slots.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the entity whose quest progress is being evaluated.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to check against the bot's active quest objectives.

doc.notes: Caller should ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking; returns true if the item contributes to completing at least one incomplete quest, false otherwise.

doc.summary: Retrieves the world object associated with a specific GUID from the perspective of a bot's AI system.
doc.overview: This function queries the bot's shadow AI instance to locate either a corpse or an active game object matching the provided GUID. It first attempts to find a creature in a dead state within the world, and if unsuccessful, searches for a spawned game object. The function returns a pointer to the found object or nullptr if no match exists.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The bot instance whose AI system is used to query the world.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The unique identifier of the object (creature or game object) to search for.

doc.notes: Relies on GET_SHADOW_AI(bot) being valid; returns nullptr if the bot lacks an AI instance. Returns a corpse only if it is currently in the world.

doc.summary: Constructs a LootObject by copying the GUID, skill ID, required skill value, and required item from another LootObject instance.
doc.overview: This function implements the copy constructor for the LootObject class, creating a new object that is an exact duplicate of the provided 'other' instance. It initializes the internal state by directly assigning values from the source object to ensure data consistency without deep copying complex structures. This operation is typically used when cloning loot definitions or preparing objects for serialization.

params.name: other
params.desc: A const reference to another LootObject instance whose properties will be copied.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure 'other' is not a dangling pointer or temporary object that might be destroyed before the copy completes, although the const reference semantics generally prevent immediate issues. Edge cases include copying objects with null pointers for reqItem, which are handled by standard C++ assignment operators.

doc.summary: Determines whether a bot player is permitted to loot a specific target based on proximity, inventory requirements, skill levels, and object state.
doc.overview: This function evaluates multiple conditions to prevent invalid looting attempts by bots, including empty stacks, missing world objects, and insufficient interaction distance. It further checks for required item counts, specific skill values, and special equipment constraints for skills like mining and skinning before returning a boolean result.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the bot player instance attempting to perform the action.

params.name: reqItem
params.desc: Optional item ID required for looting; null if no specific item is needed.

params.name: skillId
params.desc: The skill ID associated with the target object or action.

params.name: reqSkillValue
params.desc: Optional minimum skill value required to perform the action; null if none.

doc.notes: The function relies on global constants like INTERACTION_DISTANCE and specific item IDs for mining/skinning checks. It assumes valid botAI access via GET_SHADOW_AI and may return false if the target is a corpse without proper permissions or if the bot lacks necessary skills.

doc.summary: Adds a loot object to the global available loot pool, returning false if the pool is full or the insertion fails.
doc.overview: This function attempts to insert a specific ObjectGuid into the globally shared availableLoot stack. Before attempting insertion, it performs a size check and potentially shrinks or clears the stack if it exceeds MAX_LOOT_OBJECT_COUNT, ensuring the pool remains within limits. The function returns true only if the guid is successfully added; otherwise, it returns false.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The ObjectGuid representing the loot item to be added to the available pool.

doc.notes: Callers should check the return value to determine if the object was successfully queued. The function relies on global MAX_LOOT_OBJECT_COUNT and availableLoot, meaning it affects all instances using this module.

doc.summary: Removes a specific loot object from the available loot list by its GUID.
doc.overview: This function searches for an item in the global available loot pool using the provided ObjectGuid. If the item exists, it is immediately removed from the LootTargetList to prevent further distribution or use.

params.name: guid
params.desc: The unique identifier of the loot object to be removed.

doc.side_effects: Modifies global state by updating the availableLoot map.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the GUID is valid before invoking this function to avoid unnecessary lookups. This operation does not return any information about whether the item was found.

doc.summary: Clears the internal loot container by emptying its contents.
doc.overview: This function removes all items from the LootObjectStack, effectively resetting the stack to an empty state. It is typically used when a player's inventory needs to be reset or when managing temporary loot pools. The operation modifies the underlying data structure directly without returning any value.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure this is only invoked when the stack is not required to persist across game logic cycles.

doc.summary: Returns true if there is a non-empty loot object within the specified maximum distance.
doc.overview: This function determines whether a player can loot an item by checking for the nearest lootable object within a given radius. It retrieves the closest object using GetNearest and verifies its validity before returning the result. The method relies on spatial queries to efficiently locate potential targets without iterating through all objects in the world.

params.name: maxDistance
params.desc: The maximum radius (in game units) within which a loot object must exist for the function to return true.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure maxDistance is non-negative; passing zero will always return false unless an object exists exactly at the player's position. Performance depends on the efficiency of GetNearest.

doc.summary: Retrieves the nearest loot object within a specified distance, returning an empty object if no loot exists.
doc.overview: This function searches for the closest loot object relative to the current player's position using the provided maximum distance. It delegates the search logic to GetNearest and returns the result only if it contains valid data, otherwise it returns an empty LootObject.

params.name: maxDistance
params.desc: The maximum radius in game units within which to search for loot objects.

doc.notes: Callers should check if the returned object is empty before attempting to use it. The function relies on the current player's position being set prior to invocation.

doc.summary: Retrieves the nearest valid loot object within a specified distance from the bot, filtering out expired items and invalid targets.
doc.overview: This function iterates through available loot targets to identify the closest object that satisfies specific conditions. It first filters out any loot older than 30 seconds and skips targets where the calculated distance exceeds the provided maxDistance threshold or is greater than the current nearest found. The function returns a LootObject representing the closest valid target, or an empty object if no suitable loot exists.

params.name: maxDistance
params.desc: Optional maximum distance threshold; if provided, only objects within this range are considered.

doc.notes: Callers should check the return value for emptiness to avoid dereferencing invalid pointers. The function relies on WorldObject access which may fail if the target is offline or inaccessible.

It first checks if shadow AI performance monitoring is enabled; if not, it returns null immediately. doc.summary: Outputs aggregated performance statistics for ShadowAI metrics to the logs, optionally filtering by total time or per-tick intervals.
doc.overview: This function iterates through collected performance data to calculate and display detailed timing metrics such as minimum, maximum, average, and percentage distribution. It calculates the required level delta based on the bot's current level to ensure the item fits within acceptable range constraints for higher quality items.

params.name: key
params.desc: Represents the equipment slot configuration including the bot's level and item quality.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Contains the item template data such as duration, quality, bonding type, class, inventory type, and required level.

It first checks for tabards, which are always equipable, then validates weight scales and inventory types before determining valid armor subclasses per class. Finally, it returns true only if the item's subclass matches one of the allowed options.

params.name: playerclass

params.name: spec

doc.notes: The function returns false if the item is a holdable (e.g., weapon) or if the player's spec does not have a defined weight scale entry. It relies on global ItemSubclass enums and assumes valid class/spec IDs.

doc.summary: Determines the appropriate equipment slots for a weapon based on player class, spec, and item template.
doc.overview: This function evaluates whether a specific item template is eligible to be equipped in the main hand, off-hand, or ranged slot by cross-referencing the player's class and specialization against predefined weight scales. It iterates through viable inventory slots to identify available positions for the item type before checking if the corresponding weapon set weights are active for that class-spec combination.

params.name: playerclass
params.desc: The class of the player character (e.g., CLASS_WARRIOR, CLASS_PALADIN).

params.name: spec
params.desc: The specialization or spec ID of the player character.

params.name: proto
params.desc: A pointer to an ItemTemplate structure containing details such as InventoryType and item subclass.

doc.notes: The function relies on global state m_weightScales which is populated elsewhere; it returns false if no viable slots exist or if the weight scale info ID is invalid. Edge cases include players with empty inventory or specs that do not match any defined weapon sets.

doc.summary: Determines whether a specific armor item can be equipped by a player based on their class, level, and the item's template properties.
doc.overview: This function evaluates equipment eligibility by first granting automatic access to tabards and shields for Warriors, Paladins, and Shamans. It then enforces strict restrictions on plate, mail, and leather armor based on the combination of player class and level thresholds (40), while also permitting cloaks regardless of constraints. Finally, it calculates and validates item stats against class-specific requirements before returning a boolean result.

params.name: clazz
params.desc: The class ID of the character attempting to equip the item.

params.name: level
params.desc: The current level of the character, used to determine tier-specific armor restrictions.

params.name: proto
params.desc: A pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing details such as inventory type, subclass, quality, and stats.

doc.notes: The function relies on global constants for class IDs, item subclasses, inventory types, and stat thresholds. It performs a loop over item stats to aggregate values before calling CheckItemStats.

doc.summary: Determines if a specific item template is valid equipment for the given character class based on allowed weapon subclasses.
doc.overview: This function validates whether an item can be equipped by a player of a specific class by checking the item's subclass against a predefined list of permitted types. It iterates through all supported classes, returning false immediately if the item's subclass does not match any valid option for that class, and returns true only if the item passes validation for the provided class.

params.name: clazz
params.desc: The character class ID to check against.

params.name: proto
params.desc: Pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing the item's subclass and other properties.

doc.notes: The function performs a strict whitelist check; any item subclass not explicitly listed for a class will result in false. Callers should ensure proto is non-null before invoking to avoid undefined behavior.

doc.summary: Builds a comprehensive item weight scale cache by querying the Shadows database for weightscales and stats, loading vendor items from the World database, and populating loot templates from creature and game object definitions.
doc.overview: This function initializes the server's item weight system by first fetching class-specific weightscale definitions and their associated stat multipliers from the Shadows database. It then queries the World database to identify all valid vendor items and constructs a drop map by aggregating loot templates from both creature and game object templates. Finally, it iterates through the item template store to calculate specific stat weights for each item, skipping test or deprecated entries.

doc.notes: Called during server initialization or when item weight configurations change; skips items with names containing 'Test', 'Deprecated', or 'Unused'; relies on sObjectMgr and WorldDatabase being accessible.

doc.summary: Calculates the total statistical weight of an item based on its template properties and the target player's class and specialization.
doc.overview: This function determines the relative value of an item by summing weights for specific stats like armor, damage, spell power, and special modifiers. It handles unique cases such as caster-only items, weapon vellums with DPS calculations, and items with on-equip spells that apply damage or healing auras.

params.name: playerclass
params.desc: The class of the player for whom the item is being evaluated.

params.name: spec
params.desc: The specialization of the player, used to adjust stat weights based on spec-specific bonuses.

params.name: proto
params.desc: A pointer to the ItemTemplate structure containing all item properties including stats, damage values, and spell effects.

doc.notes: The function relies on global spell manager access via sSpellMgr and a static map weightStatLink for stat naming. It assumes ItemTemplate is fully populated with spell data if spells are to be processed.

doc.summary: Calculates the weight for a specific item statistic based on player class, spec, and stat name.
doc.overview: This function determines the statistical weight applied to an item's value by iterating through a predefined list of scales associated with the player's class and spec. It multiplies the configured weight factor by the provided item value if a matching statistic is found in the lookup table, otherwise it returns zero.

params.name: playerclass
params.desc: The unique identifier for the player's character class.

params.name: spec
params.desc: The specialization or subclass of the player that further refines stat scaling.

params.name: stat
params.desc: A string containing the name of the specific item statistic to look up.

params.name: value
params.desc: The numerical value of the item's statistic used in the weight calculation.

doc.notes: Returns zero if the stat name does not match any entry in the m_weightScales lookup table for the given class and spec combination.

doc.summary: Retrieves the unique quest identifier associated with a given item by searching both reward and choice reward lists across all active quest templates.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the global quest template map to locate which quest offers the specified itemId as either a standard reward or a choice reward. It performs two nested loops, one for each type of reward list, breaking early once a matching quest is found to optimize performance. The function returns the quest ID if a match exists, otherwise it returns zero.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to search for within quest reward lists.

doc.notes: Callers should verify that the returned questId is non-zero before attempting to use it. The function relies on global state (sObjectMgr) and does not modify any data structures.

doc.summary: Retrieves a list of quest IDs that offer the specified item as either a direct reward or a choice reward.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all registered quest templates to identify quests containing the provided itemId in their reward lists. It checks both standard rewards and optional choice rewards, adding matching quest IDs to the result vector upon finding a match. The function returns an empty vector if no quests contain the specified item.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to search for within quest reward lists.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure itemId is valid before invoking. The function performs a full scan of all quests, which may be inefficient in large-scale scenarios; consider caching results if the item ID remains constant.

doc.summary: Retrieves the best available item upgrade for a player based on specified equipment slot, quality, and special ability.
doc.overview: This function iterates through the global item cache to find an item that matches the player's class, level, team, and equipment requirements while offering superior stat weights compared to any previously found candidate. It validates constraints such as minimum level thresholds, team affiliation, and specific slot exclusions before comparing the potential upgrade against the current inventory or a previous selection.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose equipment is being upgraded.

params.name: spec
params.desc: String identifier for the special ability or stat set the item must support.

params.name: slot
params.desc: The specific equipment slot (e.g., head, weapon) where the new item should be placed.

params.name: quality
params.desc: Optional quality tier filter; if set, only items matching this quality are considered.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: Optional ID of the current equipped item to compare stat weights against; if omitted, compares against a default baseline.

doc.notes: Returns 0 if no suitable upgrade is found or if the player lacks the required level. The function logs informational messages regarding old and new item weights but does not modify global state.

doc.summary: Retrieves a sorted list of eligible upgrade items for a player based on their class spec, equipment slot, quality, and item ID.
doc.overview: This function filters the global item information cache to identify potential upgrades that match the specified character attributes and equipment constraints. It prioritizes items with higher stat weights relative to the current equipped item (if one exists) while enforcing strict rules regarding minimum level requirements, team affiliation, and specific slot exclusions for low-weight items.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object; if null, an empty list is returned immediately.

params.name: spec
params.desc: String identifier for the specific class specialization (e.g., 'fire', 'frost').

params.name: slot
params.desc: The equipment slot index where the item should be placed.

params.name: quality
params.desc: Optional quality filter; if non-zero, only items matching this quality are considered.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The ID of the currently equipped item; used to calculate relative stat weight for comparison.

doc.notes: The function performs a linear scan of the global itemInfoCache. It logs informational messages regarding old and new item weights if an itemId is provided or if the resulting list is non-empty.

doc.summary: Returns true if the specified item ID exists in the global item information cache.
doc.overview: This function performs a constant-time lookup of an item's metadata within the shared itemInfoCache map. It is primarily used by the RandomItemMgr to validate whether a specific item has been initialized and possesses defined statistics before attempting to retrieve its weight or other properties.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item to check for existence in the cache.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the itemId is within valid bounds before invoking this function to avoid undefined behavior. The function does not modify any global state or perform I/O operations.

doc.summary: The mod-shadows C++ module enhances server gameplay by generating intelligent AI bots with dynamic combat and non-combat strategies, alongside a comprehensive broadcasting system for guild and player interactions.
doc.body:
# mod-shadows Module Wiki

## Overview
The **mod-shadows** module is a high-performance C++ extension designed to augment World of Warcraft servers with intelligent NPC bots. It operates by analyzing player classes, talents, and spec tabs to generate context-aware AI behaviors. The module manages three distinct operational states: combat, non-combat (idle), and dead, each utilizing specialized strategy engines. Additionally, it provides a robust broadcasting infrastructure that allows bots to interact with the chat system based on game events.

## How It Works
The core logic flows through the `AiFactory` class, which acts as the central orchestrator. When a bot is instantiated, `AiFactory::createAiObjectContext` determines the player's class and spec tab to initialize a specific AI object context (e.g., `PriestAiObjectContext`). Subsequently, depending on the game state, the factory creates an appropriate engine:

1.  **Combat State**: `createCombatEngine` initializes an `Engine` object and applies default combat strategies via `AddDefaultCombatStrategies`. This function checks if the player is in a battleground; if not, it adds universal strategies like "racials" and "chat". It also evaluates spec tabs to assign roles (e.g., Shadow Priest as DPS or Healer).
2.  **Non-Combat State**: `createNonCombatEngine` creates an idle engine. `AddDefaultNonCombatStrategies` configures behaviors based on the bot's role, such as "dps assist" for healers or "bthreat" for paladins.
3.  **Dead State**: `createDeadEngine` handles post-combat behavior. `AddDefaultDeadStrategies` sets up "dead", "stay", and "follow" strategies, with logic to remove the "follow" strategy if the bot is a random player without a group.

The `BroadcastHelper` class manages communication. It checks global configuration flags (e.g., `sShadowAIConfig->enableBroadcasts`) before executing events like loot notifications, quest updates, or guild promotions. Messages utilize placeholder variables (e.g., `%item_link`, `%area_name`) which are resolved dynamically.

## Key Functions and Classes

### AiFactory
The primary factory class responsible for bot lifecycle management.

| Function | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `createAiObjectContext` | Initializes the AI context based on player class, returning specific subclasses like `MageAiObjectContext` or `WarlockAiObjectContext`. |
| `GetPlayerSpecTab` | Determines the active spec tab by analyzing the bot's talent map and level. Defaults to Frost Mage if no talents are selected at level 10+. |
| `GetPlayerSpecTabs` | Retrieves a map of available spec tabs for a player, iterating through their talent map to calculate probabilities. |
| `IsFeralTank` | Checks if a Druid is in Feral form or has specific auras (e.g., `HasAura(16931)`), returning true only if the bot is configured as a Feral Tank. |
| `GetPlayerRoles` | Assigns a `BotRoles` enum value based on class and spec tab (e.g., Warrior Tab 2 = Tank). |
| `GetPlayerSpecName` | Returns a string identifier for the bot's specialization (e.g., "shadow", "resto"). |

### BroadcastHelper
Handles all chat-related broadcasting logic.

| Function | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `BroadcastToChannelWithGlobalChance` | The main dispatcher. It rolls against a global chance (`broadcastChanceMaxValue`) and specific channel chances (e.g., Guild, Trade). |
| `BroadcastLootingItem` | Triggers when a bot loots an item, formatting the item link via `%item_link`. |
| `BroadcastQuestUpdateAddKill` | Notifies players when a bot adds a kill to a quest, using placeholders for area and zone names. |
| `BroadcastGuildMemberPromotion` | Announces guild member promotions with dynamic class/race formatting. |

## Configuration and Usage
Server operators configure the module via `sShadowAIConfig`. Key options control whether broadcasting is active and the probability of specific events occurring.

### Core Configuration Keys

| Option Name | Default Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `enableBroadcasts` | `true` | Global flag to enable or disable all bot chat broadcasts. |
| `broadcastChanceMaxValue` | `100` | The maximum value for the random roll used to determine if a broadcast event triggers. |
| `broadcastToGuildGlobalChance` | `50` | Chance (out of 100) that a bot will attempt to broadcast to the Guild channel globally. |
| `broadcastChanceQuestAccepted` | `20` | Chance for a bot to announce when they accept a quest. |
| `broadcastChanceGuildManagement` | `30` | Chance for a bot to announce guild member promotions or demotions. |

### Usage Example

#### 1. Configuration File Snippet
Add the following options to your server's configuration file (e.g., `ShadowAIConfig.ini` or equivalent) to enable and tune broadcasting:

```ini
[ShadowAI]
enableBroadcasts = true
broadcastChanceMaxValue = 100
broadcastToGuildGlobalChance = 50
broadcastChanceQuestAccepted = 20
broadcastChanceGuildManagement = 30
```

#### 2. Injected Content File
When a bot loots an item, the module injects the following formatted string into the chat system (assuming `enableBroadcasts` is true and the roll succeeds):

```text
[Bot] You found %item_link in %area_name.
```

*Note: If `enableBroadcasts` is set to false, this function returns immediately without sending any message.*

doc.summary: Retrieves the minimum level required to obtain a specific item from the global cache, returning zero if the item is not found.
doc.overview: This function queries the centralized item information cache to determine the lowest character level at which an item can be acquired. It performs a direct lookup using the provided item ID and returns the stored minimum level value or zero if the entry does not exist in the cache.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item for which the minimum acquisition level is being queried.

doc.notes: Callers should verify that the returned value is non-zero before attempting to use it for validation logic; a return of zero indicates the item has no cached level data.

doc.summary: Retrieves the statistical weight for a specific item based on the player's class and selected special ability.
doc.overview: This function calculates an item's stat weight by first validating that both the player and item exist, then looking up the item's associated weights in a cache. It determines the correct special ability ID by comparing the player's current spec name against a list of available scales for their class, returning zero if no valid combination is found or if the item lacks defined weights.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose special ability and class determine the weight calculation.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item for which the stat weight is being queried.

doc.notes: Returns 0 if the player or itemId is null, the item is not cached, the player has no spec name, or no matching special ability weight exists for the given class and spec.

doc.summary: Calculates the live statistical weight for a specific item based on player class, spec, level, team, and quest status.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the appropriate weight scale for an item by first validating that both the player and item ID are present. It then checks the player's current spec against available weight scales to determine the correct spec ID, ensuring the item is not locked due to level restrictions, team affiliation, or specific source requirements like quests or PvP honor points.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose stats and inventory are being evaluated.

params.name: itemId
params.desc: The unique identifier of the item for which the weight is being calculated.

doc.notes: Returns 0 if the player has no active spec, the item level exceeds the player's level, the team does not match, or specific source conditions (quests/PvP) are unmet.

doc.summary: BuildEquipCache constructs a lookup table mapping equipment slots and qualities to item IDs for all playable classes and levels, either by querying an existing database record or by generating entries on the fly.
doc.overview: This function initializes the server's equipment cache by iterating through all valid player classes and level/quality combinations. It first attempts to retrieve pre-computed data from the Shadows database; if no records exist, it dynamically generates the cache by evaluating item templates against class-specific equip rules and inserting new entries into the database.
doc.notes: Called during server initialization or cache refresh; handles edge cases where no playable classes exist or the database is empty.

For each entity, it captures detailed attributes including position (WKT format), orientation, race, class, map ID, level, health, power percentage, money, combat status, and specific AI state flags if applicable. The function handles potential exceptions by silently returning without side effects.
doc.notes: Callsers should ensure the ShadowAIConfig singleton is properly initialized before invoking this function. Edge case: If an exception occurs during logging, the function exits early without clearing the file or performing cleanup.

It calculates the maximum allowed bot count based on event values or random ranges, then determines focus levels based on online bot counts. The core logic handles bot spawning, initialization states, and checks for real player presence to enforce login delays or logout conditions.

It then loads current shadow account type assignments into memory to identify which accounts are already categorized. The logic calculates the required number of RNDbot and AddClass accounts based on global configuration settings, including periodic online/offline ratios, and proceeds to assign types 1 and 2 respectively to any unassigned accounts in the database.

Based on this maximum, it calculates and sets the starting level for random bots, ensuring they do not exceed the top player's level by more than three.

doc.summary: Schedules a randomization event for the specified bot at the given timestamp.
doc.overview: This function registers an event within the RandomShadowMgr system to trigger a randomization action for a specific bot. It stores the event details, including the bot identifier and the scheduled time, allowing the game server to execute the randomization logic when that time arrives.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot to be randomized.

params.name: time
params.desc: The timestamp at which the randomization event should occur.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot ID is valid before invoking this function. The time parameter is treated as an absolute timestamp relative to the server's clock.

doc.summary: Schedules a teleport event for a specific bot at a calculated or provided future timestamp.
doc.overview: This function calculates the target time for a teleport event if none is explicitly provided, defaulting to a random interval between 60 seconds and three times the configured random update interval. It then sets an internal event value associated with the bot's ID and the 'teleport' key, marking the scheduled occurrence.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot to be teleported.

params.name: time
params.desc: The timestamp when the teleport should occur; if zero, a random interval is generated instead.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot exists before invoking this function. The 'time' parameter acts as a flag where 0 triggers automatic calculation based on configuration.

doc.summary: Schedules a random strategy change for the specified bot at the given or default time.
doc.overview: This function triggers a strategy change event for a specific bot by setting an internal event value. If no valid time is provided, it automatically calculates a random duration within the configured minimum and maximum bounds defined in sShadowAIConfig. The operation relies on the SetEventValue helper to register the event without performing any blocking I/O or modifying global state.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot whose strategy is being scheduled to change.

params.name: time
params.desc: The timestamp at which the strategy change should occur; defaults to a random value if zero or invalid.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure 'bot' is a valid bot ID. The function does not perform network operations or lock external resources.

doc.summary: Processes a bot's lifecycle events including initialization, randomization, teleportation, and logout based on stored event values.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the player associated with a given bot ID and checks for specific event flags to determine the required action. If the bot is initializing or has not been added yet, it schedules random updates, potential randomization, and teleportation before returning success. For active bots in the world, it validates their state against group membership and flight status before processing AI logic and scheduling revives.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot to process.

doc.side_effects: Network (LogoutShadow), Global State (currentBots modification, EventValue updates)
doc.notes: Returns false if the bot is invalid, not in world, or flagged for logout without an active update event.

doc.summary: Processes a bot's AI state to handle death reviving, group management, and idle randomization/teleportation based on event values.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the bot's shadow AI instance and checks if it is currently in a battleground or queue, returning false if so. It then evaluates the bot's status for death, group leadership conflicts, and idle states to determine whether to trigger randomization or teleportation events.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot to be processed.

doc.notes: Calls GetShadowAI, Revive, Randomize, Refresh, and RandomTeleportForLevel; modifies event values for dead/revive/randomize/teleport states.

doc.summary: Revives a player by resetting their death event state and triggering refresh and teleport mechanics.
doc.overview: This function initiates the revival process for a specific player by first generating a unique bot identifier based on the player's GUID counter. It then updates two internal event values to mark the player as revived, followed by refreshing the player's status and applying a random teleport effect appropriate for their current level.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object being revived.

doc.side_effects: Internal state modification via SetEventValue; calls Refresh and RandomTeleportGrindForLevel.
doc.notes: Caller must ensure player is alive or handle preconditions appropriately. Edge case: Player GUID counter uniqueness should be maintained by the underlying system.

doc.summary: Teleports a bot to a randomly selected valid location from a provided list, skipping invalid targets based on game state and map constraints.
doc.overview: This function attempts to teleport a bot to one of the locations specified in the input vector by filtering out invalid positions and shuffling the remaining candidates. It performs extensive validation checks before execution, including verifying the bot's current state, ensuring it is not in a battleground or arena, and confirming the location is accessible based on map data, zone teams, water levels, and ground height.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the bot entity to be teleported.

params.name: locs
params.desc: A vector of WorldLocation objects containing potential target coordinates and map IDs for teleportation.

params.name: hearth
params.desc: Boolean flag indicating whether to set the bot's homebind location upon successful teleport.

doc.notes: The function returns early if the bot is being teleported, not in the world, in a battleground/arena, or if it is not a group leader. It also skips locations that are filtered out by shadow AI configuration, located in water, on invalid ground height, or within prohibited zone teams relative to the bot's faction.

doc.side_effects: Global state modification via `zone2LevelBracket` array and potential I/O if `sShadowAIConfig` is derived from external data.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure this function is invoked before any logic depends on the populated bracket map; edge cases include missing entries in `sShadowAIConfig` which will simply not overwrite existing hardcoded values.

Additionally, if enabled, it processes innkeepers and flightmasters to populate specific zone-based caches.

doc.summary: RandomTeleportForLevel teleports a bot to a random location within its level's starter cache or banker locations based on faction alignment and configurable weights.
doc.overview: This function determines the appropriate teleport target for a bot by first checking if it is currently in a battleground, returning early if so. It then selects between standard starter locations and specialized banker locations depending on whether the new RPG strategy is enabled and the bot's level. If the bot reaches level 10 and a random probability check passes, the function attempts to select a banker location based on faction alignment or weighted city preferences before falling back to standard locations.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot to be teleported.

doc.side_effects: Network (teleport execution), Global state (uses static configuration and cache maps)
doc.notes: Relies on external caches like allianceStarterPerLevelCache, hordeStarterPerLevelCache, bankerLocsPerLevelCache, and cityToBankers. Uses urand for random selection and sShadowAIConfig for strategy flags and weights.

doc.summary: RandomTeleportGrindForLevel teleports a player bot to a random starting location based on its level and race if it is not currently in a battleground.
doc.overview: This function checks if the provided bot is inside a battleground; if so, it returns immediately without action. Otherwise, it retrieves the bot's current level and race to determine which pool of valid starting locations to use, selecting between new RPG strategy caches or legacy caches depending on configuration. Finally, it logs a debug message with relevant details before executing the teleportation.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the player bot instance to be teleported.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure the bot is a valid player instance. Edge case: If the bot's level exceeds the bounds of the configured location caches, behavior is undefined.

doc.summary: Initiates a random teleport for the specified bot unit, optionally using nearby targets to calculate a new position or falling back to level-based logic.
doc.overview: This function checks if the bot is currently in a battleground and returns early if true. It then attempts to find valid target units within a configured distance range; if targets exist, it calculates a destination based on those targets using the FleeManager, otherwise it delegates to RandomTeleportForLevel. Finally, it records performance metrics and refreshes the bot's state.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the bot unit instance that is being teleported.

doc.side_effects: Performance monitoring, potential network refresh via Refresh(), and internal state updates.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot pointer is valid. If no targets are found within range, the function automatically invokes RandomTeleportForLevel.

doc.summary: Randomize determines the initial randomization state for a bot player based on their current battleground status, level, and class.
doc.overview: This function checks if the bot is currently in a battleground; if so, it exits early without modification. For bots outside battlegrounds, it applies specific logic depending on the bot's level and class: Death Knights below level 56 are randomized via RandomizeFirst, while other classes follow standard Shadow AI randomization rules unless configured otherwise.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot whose randomization state is being determined.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot is not in a battleground before invoking this function to avoid unnecessary processing. Edge case: Death Knights at level 56 or higher will use standard Shadow AI randomization unless sShadowAIConfig->downgradeMaxLevelBot is set.

doc.summary: Increments the level of a bot player and updates its shadow attributes if the level changes.
doc.overview: This function retrieves the maximum allowed level for random bots from configuration, clamping it against the world's global max player level. It calculates the new level by incrementing the current one, then checks if this change differs from the previous level to determine if a ShadowFactory instance is needed for randomization.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the bot player object whose level is being increased.

doc.side_effects: Performance monitoring operations; potential ShadowFactory instantiation and randomization.
doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking. Edge case: if the calculated new level equals the current level, no shadow factory instance is created.

doc.summary: RandomizeFirst determines a random level for a bot player based on configuration rules and applies the new level to the Shadow AI.
doc.overview: This function first validates that the bot has an associated Shadow AI before proceeding. It calculates a target level by checking global configurations, class-specific requirements (such as Death Knights), and specific flags like downgrade or disable random levels. After selecting the appropriate level, it updates the bot's internal state via SetValue, creates a new Shadow instance with the randomized level, and executes database updates to record the randomization time and logout status.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot whose level is being randomized.

doc.side_effects: Database writes (ShadowsDatabase), Shadow instance creation, Performance monitoring operations, and potential group disbandment.
doc.notes: The function relies on GET_SHADOW_AI to retrieve the bot's AI object; if this fails, it returns early. It uses urand for randomization logic and interacts with global configuration structures like sShadowAIConfig and sWorld.

doc.summary: RandomizeMin resets a bot's AI state and updates its shadow database records with randomized time intervals for randomization and in-world presence.
doc.overview: This function initializes the bot's AI configuration by setting the minimum level based on global settings and then triggers a randomization process. It generates two random durations using configured min/max ranges to determine when the bot should next randomize and when it should be considered present in the world, storing these values directly into the ShadowsDatabase. Finally, the function resets the internal AI state and handles group membership before finishing performance monitoring.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot whose AI is being randomized.

doc.side_effects: Database writes (ShadowsDatabase), Performance monitoring operations, AI state reset, potential group disbanding.
doc.notes: Requires valid botAI via GET_SHADOW_AI; returns early if invalid. Relies on global configuration sShadowAIConfig and sPerformanceMonitor.

doc.summary: Clears all shadow-related data for the specified player by instantiating a ShadowFactory and invoking its ClearEverything method.
doc.overview: This function removes all shadows associated with a specific player from the game world. It creates a temporary ShadowFactory instance initialized with the player's current level, then delegates the cleanup task to the factory's ClearEverything method.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose shadows are to be cleared.

doc.notes: The function relies on the ShadowFactory constructor accepting a level parameter derived from the player's state.

doc.summary: Determines a random valid player level for a creature based on the map ID and a specified teleport location.
doc.overview: This function queries the database to find the minimum and maximum creature levels within a specific map area defined by the provided coordinates. It then selects a random level between these bounds, falling back to a random level up to the global maximum if no creatures are found in the vicinity.

params.name: mapId
params.desc: The unique identifier for the game map where the creature will spawn.

params.name: teleX
params.desc: The X-coordinate of the teleport location used to define the search radius around the creature's position.

params.name: teleY
params.desc: The Y-coordinate of the teleport location used to define the search radius around the creature's position.

doc.notes: The function relies on global configuration for maximum player level and random bot teleport distance; callers should ensure the map ID corresponds to an existing creature template.

doc.summary: Resets a player bot's AI, health, resources, and group status while skipping dead or battleground entities.
doc.overview: This function refreshes the state of a player bot by first checking if the entity is alive and not in a battleground. If the bot is dead, it resurrects them and resets their strategies; otherwise, it logs the operation, measures performance, and executes a comprehensive reset including AI strategy, durability, health, power levels, money, and group affiliation.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player entity representing the bot whose state is being refreshed.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot pointer is valid. The function returns early if the bot is dead or in a battleground, so these conditions should be checked by callers if pre-validation is required.

doc.summary: Determines whether a given player is a random bot by checking their AI type and GUID counter.
doc.overview: This function first attempts to identify if the provided player has a Shadow AI instance associated with them. If such an AI exists, it checks whether the player is a real human; if so, the function returns false immediately. If no Shadow AI is found or the player object is null, the function falls back to checking the player's GUID counter against a known list of random bot counters.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object to be evaluated.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking this function. The GUID counter check relies on pre-populated data and may return false positives if a new random bot GUID has not yet been registered in the system.

doc.summary: Determines whether a given player GUID is currently classified as a random bot based on account configuration and an active bot list.
doc.overview: This function checks if the provided player GUID corresponds to an account listed in the shadow AI's random account configuration. If the account is not in that list, it immediately returns false. Otherwise, it verifies whether the specific GUID exists within the current list of active bots before returning a final result.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The ObjectGuid::LowType identifier of the player to check.

doc.notes: Relies on sShadowAIConfig and sCharacterCache being initialized; returns false if the GUID is not found in either the random account list or the current bots list.

doc.summary: Determines whether a given player is an AddClass bot by checking their AI type or GUID counter.
doc.overview: This function first attempts to retrieve the shadow AI associated with the provided player. If the AI exists and represents a real player, it returns false immediately. Otherwise, it falls back to checking the player's GUID counter to determine if they are an AddClass bot, returning true only if the counter indicates such a status.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object to inspect.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking this function. The function relies on GET_SHADOW_AI() and IsAddclassBot() being implemented correctly for accurate results.

doc.summary: Determines whether a given player GUID is classified as an AddClass bot by checking class addition caches and account types.
doc.overview: This function iterates through all valid game classes except the Mage (class 10) to verify if the provided GUID exists in the addclass cache for any alliance or faction. If no match is found in the cache, it checks the character's account type to see if it matches the criteria for an AddClass bot.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The ObjectGuid::LowType identifier of the player to check.

doc.notes: Relies on sCharacterCache and addclassCache global state; returns true if the GUID is found in class addition caches or belongs to an account type flagged as 2.

doc.summary: Retrieves a list of random bots for the current event, populating the global currentBots container up to a configured maximum count.
doc.overview: This function queries the ShadowsDatabase for bot IDs associated with the current event and owner. It fetches results from a prepared statement, validates each bot against the 'add' flag, and appends valid bots to the currentBots vector until the maximum allowed count is reached or no more rows exist.
doc.notes: Caller must ensure currentBots is empty before invoking; returns early if already populated. Edge case: maxAllowedBotCount set to 0 prevents any bots from being added.

doc.summary: Retrieves a list of background bot IDs from the Shadows database filtered by a specific bracket identifier.
doc.overview: This function queries the Shadows database for random background bots associated with the provided bracket using a prepared statement. It iterates through the query results, extracting the bot ID from each row and populating a vector that is returned to the caller.

params.name: bracket
params.desc: The unique identifier of the tournament bracket for which background bots are requested.

doc.side_effects: Database query execution and potential I/O operations.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the returned vector is not empty before processing. The function relies on the existence of the SHADOWS_SEL_RANDOM_BOTS_BY_EVENT_AND_VALUE prepared statement in the ShadowsDatabase module.

doc.summary: Retrieves the current value for a specific event associated with a given bot, caching results and handling expiration logic.
doc.overview: This function first checks if an event cache entry exists for the specified bot; if not, it queries the ShadowsDatabase to populate the cache. It then retrieves the cached event data, validates its freshness against the current time, and returns the event value unless the event is a special type like 'specNo' or 'specLink'.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot for which the event value is being retrieved.

params.name: event
params.desc: A string representing the name of the event whose value is requested.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure 'bot' and 'event' are valid. Returns 0 if the event has expired or is a special type.

doc.summary: Retrieves the cached event data string for a specific bot and event identifier.
doc.overview: This function queries the internal event cache to fetch pre-stored data associated with a given bot ID and event name. It first checks if an entry exists for the provided parameters using GetEventValue, then returns the stored data string from the cache map if found, otherwise returning an empty string.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot requesting the event data.

params.name: event
params.desc: A string containing the specific event name or key to look up in the cache.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure bot and event identifiers are valid before calling. Returns empty string if no cached data exists for the given parameters.

doc.summary: Sets a random shadow bot's event value in the database and updates the local cache.
doc.overview: This function initiates a database transaction to either delete or insert records for a specific bot and event combination. If the provided value is non-zero, it inserts a new record containing the current game time, validity period, and optional data string; otherwise, it prepares a deletion query. After committing the transaction, the function updates the local event cache with the new state.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot to modify.

params.name: event
params.desc: A string representing the name of the event associated with the bot.

params.name: value
params.desc: The value to set; if non-zero, a new record is inserted, otherwise a deletion is prepared.

params.name: validIn
params.desc: The timestamp indicating when the event validity period begins.

params.name: data
params.desc: An optional string containing additional metadata for the event record.

doc.side_effects: Database transaction (write/delete), local cache update, potential I/O via database connection.
doc.notes: Returns the original value argument. The 'data' parameter is optional and defaults to an empty string if not provided.

doc.summary: Retrieves the event value associated with a specific bot and event type.
doc.overview: This function acts as a thin wrapper that delegates the actual retrieval logic to GetEventValue. It is primarily used within the RandomShadowMgr module to fetch dynamic values based on bot identifiers and predefined event categories. The implementation relies entirely on the underlying GetEventValue function, which handles the core data access.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot for which the value is being requested.

params.name: type
params.desc: A string constant representing the specific event type to query.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot ID and event type are valid before invoking this function to avoid potential errors in GetEventValue. Edge cases include bots that have been removed or event types that do not exist in the system.

doc.summary: Delegates the random shadow value retrieval to the core logic by converting the player's GUID counter into a unique identifier.
doc.overview: This function acts as a thin wrapper that forwards the request to the primary GetValue implementation, ensuring thread safety and uniqueness based on the bot's GUID. It avoids direct interaction with global state or network I/O by relying entirely on the internal counter mechanism of the player object. The operation is lightweight and designed for high-frequency calls within the game loop.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the bot instance.

params.name: type
params.desc: String identifier specifying the type of random shadow value to retrieve.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot pointer is valid before invoking this function. Edge cases include bots with invalid GUIDs, which may result in undefined behavior if GetCounter fails.

doc.summary: Retrieves a specific event data string for the given bot and event type.
doc.overview: This function acts as a thin wrapper that delegates the actual retrieval logic to GetEventData. It accepts a bot identifier and an event type string, returning the corresponding data as a const reference to a std::string.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot for which the data is being requested.

params.name: type
params.desc: A string specifying the type of event data to retrieve.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot ID and type are valid before invoking this function, as GetEventData may return an empty string or throw exceptions based on internal validation.

doc.summary: Sets the random shadow event value for a specific bot based on its type and provided data.
doc.overview: This function acts as a thin wrapper that forwards configuration parameters to the core event logic. It retrieves the maximum allowed time for random bots in the world from the global AI configuration before delegating the actual value setting operation. The implementation ensures thread safety by accessing shared state through the configured singleton instance.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier of the bot whose shadow event is being modified.

params.name: type
params.desc: A string specifying the category or kind of the random shadow event.

params.name: value
params.desc: The integer value to be assigned to the shadow event for the specified bot.

params.name: data
params.desc: Additional string information associated with the event configuration.

doc.notes: Callers must ensure the bot ID is valid before invoking this function to avoid undefined behavior in the underlying SetEventValue call.

doc.summary: This function acts as a thin wrapper that forwards player-specific random shadow settings to the global RandomShadowMgr.
doc.overview: The SetValue function accepts a Player pointer and converts it into a GUID counter before delegating the actual configuration update to the centralized RandomShadowMgr. This design ensures that individual player data is processed through a shared manager while maintaining encapsulation of the core logic. It is primarily used by game entities requiring dynamic random shadow adjustments based on player input.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object whose GUID counter will be used as the key for the configuration.

params.name: type
params.desc: A string identifier specifying the category or kind of random shadow setting being configured.

params.name: value
params.desc: An unsigned 32-bit integer representing the numerical value for the specified type.

params.name: data
params.desc: A string containing additional metadata or context associated with the random shadow setting.

doc.notes: Callers should ensure the Player pointer is valid before invoking this function. The actual logic resides in RandomShadowMgr::SetValue, which uses bot->GetGUID().GetCounter() as the unique identifier.

doc.summary: Executes a console command to manage random shadow bots, handling specific actions like reset, stats, reload, update, or invoking sub-commands for individual bot operations.
doc.overview: This function serves as the central dispatcher for all console commands related to the Random Shadow system. It first validates that the Shadows feature is enabled and that an argument string was provided, returning false if either check fails. Depending on the command name, it performs specific actions such as resetting the bot database, printing statistics, reloading configuration, or iterating through registered handlers to apply custom logic to player bots.

params.name: handler
params.desc: The ChatHandler instance executing the command; marked as unused.

params.name: args
params.desc: A null-terminated C-string containing the command name (e.g., 'reset', 'stats') or a sub-command with optional arguments.

doc.side_effects: Database queries, global state modification (config reload), logging, and potential network I/O via ChatHandler.
doc.notes: Returns false if the Shadows system is disabled or if no valid command argument is provided. The 'reset' command requires a server restart to take effect. Sub-commands like 'init', 'clear', and 'levelup' are parsed by iterating through registered handlers and applying them to all matching random bots.

doc.summary: Iterates through all shadow bots to dispatch specific command types and text payloads to their respective AI handlers.
doc.overview: This function acts as a central dispatcher for commands originating from the player or channel system, routing them to individual bot instances. It first filters bots based on team-specific channel membership if a channel name is provided, ensuring that only relevant bots receive the command. Each matching bot's internal AI logic then processes the command type and text data.

params.name: type
params.desc: The integer identifier representing the specific command category or action to be executed.

params.name: text
params.desc: A string containing the payload or arguments associated with the command.

params.name: fromPlayer
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object that initiated the command, used for logging or context within bot AI.

params.name: channelName
params.desc: Optional string identifying a specific communication channel; if empty, all bots are considered.

doc.notes: The function relies on external snapshot data via GetShadowsSnapshot() and internal AI pointers obtained through GET_SHADOW_AI(). It does not perform direct I/O or modify global state outside of the bot instances.

doc.summary: Removes a player from the active player list and cleans up their associated bot AI instances.
doc.overview: This function handles the cleanup logic when a player logs out by first disabling their shadow instance via GUID. It then iterates through all registered bot AIs to identify any bots controlled by the logging-out player, resetting their master reference and strategies if they are not in a battleground. Finally, it searches for and removes the player object from the global players vector.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player instance that is logging out.

doc.side_effects: Global state (modifies the 'players' vector); Network (triggers logout events via player removal).
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the player is in a valid state before calling. Edge case: If the player pointer is invalid or null, behavior is undefined.

doc.summary: Logs bot login events and manages XP gain flags based on shadow count limits and AI configuration.
doc.overview: This function records the login of a bot to the server's shadow management system, logging the current count against the maximum allowed limit. It then conditionally applies or removes the no-XP-gain flag depending on whether the random bot level is fixed in the active configuration.

params.name: bot
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object representing the logging in bot.

doc.notes: Caller must ensure the bot is valid; edge case occurs when shadow count reaches maximum limit, disabling further bot logins.

doc.summary: OnPlayerLogin initializes a player's shadow AI master and handles teleportation logic for players near excessive bot counts.
doc.overview: This function is invoked when a player logs in to establish their connection with nearby shadow bots, specifically setting them as masters if they are not already controlled by another bot. It iterates through a snapshot of all shadow bots to find the nearest available master candidate within the same group. Additionally, it checks for conditions where more than 100 bots are nearby; if met and the player lacks a faction template, it teleports them to a random point, otherwise selecting a destination based on faction reputation.

params.name: player
params.desc: Pointer to the Player object that has just logged in.

doc.notes: Calls player->TeleportTo which may interrupt active auras; relies on global configuration sShadowAIConfig and sTravelMgr for destination logic.

doc.summary: Removes a specific bot from the active list and clears its associated event value upon player login failure.
doc.overview: This function is invoked when a player fails to log in, specifically targeting bots that were attempting to connect. It first resets the event value for the specified bot ID to zero, ensuring any pending game logic related to that bot is cleared. Subsequently, it removes the bot's identifier from the global list of currently active bots using an erase-remove idiom.

params.name: bot
params.desc: The unique identifier (uint32) of the bot player to be removed and reset.

doc.side_effects: Global state modification via list erasure; event value reset.
doc.notes: Callers should ensure the bot ID is valid before invoking. Edge case: If the bot was never added to currentBots, the erase operation will have no effect.

doc.summary: Returns a random player from the current player list or null if no players exist.
doc.overview: This function retrieves a randomly selected player instance from the internal player collection. It first checks if the player list is empty, returning nullptr immediately if so, otherwise it generates a random index within valid bounds and returns the corresponding player object.
doc.notes: Callers must handle the possibility of receiving nullptr to avoid dereferencing errors. The randomness is determined by the global urand function, which may have its own seeding behavior.
